video_title: Wolves Logo Reveal | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on the Timberwolves' potential for an NBA championship
quotes.excerpt: the fact that they're knocking on the door for an NBA championship
quotes.quote: It's exciting, you know, when you look at where this team has gone, the fact that they're knocking on the door for an NBA championship. And I still say, and I look, I picked San Antonio and New York to play in the finals, I picked New York to win it months back, but I honestly believe if Anthony Edwards was healthy, because what people don't understand, he makes everybody on this team 4 to 5 to 6% better. And it's those little incremental things that you need to get over the hump. Him not being able to perform at his maximum really hurt this team.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on why the Timberwolves struggle against teams like the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: you're not going to beat the Knicks playing three four guards
quotes.quote: San Antonio was put together to mirror OKC. They play a bunch of guards. Look at their draft, all guards. You're not going to beat the Knicks playing three four guards. When this team is healthy, you're not going to beat this team with three or four guards because you got to figure it out. The reason I took the Knicks to take away the team is constructed. San Antonio was constructed to beat one team, OKC. They did it. They have no clue when you look at OG Anunoby, Jalen Brunson, those bookend forwards, 6'10, 6'7, that's size and they're skilled and they're quick and they're athletic and they can shoot.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Jaden McDaniels' potential to improve offensively
quotes.excerpt: I think Jaden McDaniels can get even better. I think he can become a better scorer
quotes.quote: Everybody keep talking about adding something. I want to put a little pressure on Jaden McDaniels. I think Jaden McDaniels can get even better. I think he can become a better scorer. Now he's already a great defender, but I think offensively, he's only on the scratch of the surface of his talent. And if I was Anthony Edwards, I'd put my arms around him and say, while they out there looking for that number two scorer, he's right there. You saw some of the games he had in the playoffs. He's capable. You just got to instill in him, and early in the season, he may have some clunkers, but you got to spoon feed him and get him in that mindset of being a scorer and I think he can do it.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Anthony Edwards' potential as a modern NBA player
quotes.excerpt: He is the modern day NBA player when you look at the metrics
quotes.quote: At his size and skill set, who can guard him? He's 6'9, 6'10, close to 6'10, he can handle, he can shoot, he can defend. He is the modern day NBA player when you look at the metrics. And all you got to do, and it's hard to go from being a 16 point scorer to 22 points. People don't understand that, it's mindset. You almost got to not have a conscious. You almost got to not care when you have bad games. But as a coach, they got to instill in him that. His teammates can help with that by encouraging him, by sometimes deflecting when they have a shot, giving it to him.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on why he defends Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's playstyle
quotes.excerpt: You're taught as a player to get away with what you can get away with
quotes.quote: You're taught as a player to get away with what you can get away with. That's why you have three officials. So for all the people to be mad at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, get mad at the people who make the call. If I can get to the free throw line 17 times and as a coach he can do that, why am I going to encourage him to stop? The officials are going to make the call. Yes, that's what you got three officials for. So they got to do their job. So I don't, it doesn't bother me what Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is doing because it's working.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Bill Musselman's coaching philosophy
quotes.excerpt: I'd rather die and lose because at least when you're dead, you're dead
quotes.quote: Bill Musselman was so driven about winning. I remember he used to say to us, you know, I'd rather die and lose because at least when you're dead, you're dead. If you live, you got to live with losing. That's how he thought, right? And he instilled that in us and we won 29 games that first year and we were in every game. I remember we were playing Portland and that's when they were really good and Kevin Duckworth, God bless the dead, he yelled out, I hate playing y'all. I just hate it because we were going to hold the ball, we were going to play tough defense, we were going to keep the game in the high 80s or 90s and try to win it.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on his reunion with Kevin Garnett
quotes.excerpt: He picked me up off my feet and hugged me. It was great, man
quotes.quote: I have talked to Kevin Garnett, but I haven't physically seen him in years. And I went up to his hotel room and didn't tell him I was coming. And they gave me a key, so I'm starting to use the key going to his room. He's yelling, oh, who's coming in? And when I walk through the door, he picked me up off my feet and hugged me. It was great, man, because he's the heart and soul. The reason these guys play the way they play, yeah, it's the city, it's the organization, but who put all that in place? He did, his mentality. He left it on that court every day. You saw him every night.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Kevin Garnett's loyalty to the Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: Kevin McHale had to sit him down and make him accept the trade
quotes.quote: Kevin McHale had to sit him down and make him accept the trade. He did not want to leave here. He was like, look, I'm going to win a championship here, I'm not going to win one. He was loyal to a fault to this organization. And Kevin McHale, you know, when he laid it out for him, he's, and I remember the conversation, you don't want to be one of those players the greatest to not want a championship. And I think Kevin Garnett respects that and understands that, but I, I can tell you 100%, he much rather have won this championship here in Minnesota.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Kevin Garnett's superstitions
quotes.excerpt: Kevin Garnett was very superstitious about everything
quotes.quote: First of all, Kevin Garnett was very superstitious about everything. Everything before every game had to go in the certain order at a certain time. What he ate, what he drank, the way the hot packs were put on his knees. Clayton Wilson, our equipment manager, had to write something on his tape ankles before every game at a certain time. Like, it was routine. So he had this thing about a two dollar bill putting in his socks. Some kind, and I collect them. What he didn't realize, he didn't know that. So when he lost the two dollar bill, for some reason, Clayton was like, Clayton was always in our stuff. He was stirring the pot. Clayton like, KG, Mitch got a bunch of two dollar bills. I guarantee he found yours.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Kevin Garnett's intense focus during games
quotes.excerpt: He would not play. I remember a game Clayton was busy, couldn't write on his tape
quotes.quote: He would not play. I remember a game Clayton was busy, couldn't write on his tape. KG called a timeout two minutes into the game. Flip like, what are you? Flip, I got to get Clayton. Clayton, come write on my tape. And Flip just, just shook his head because he understood he was not going to be right until he, KG wrote whatever he writes on his ankles.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on why he benched Karl-Anthony Towns as a rookie
quotes.excerpt: I need to teach this young man how to play the right way, play defense
quotes.quote: I need to teach this young man how to play the right way, play defense. What were those early days with Cat like just trying to get him settled in as a rookie, figuring out the right way to play and get established here? He was awesome. First of all, he's a unbelievable, nice young man. Just exceptional. He loves basketball. He cares about his teammates. It was easy to coach Cat. Now, the thing you have to do with a guy that talented, every now and then, you got to rein him in a little bit. You just have to rein him in a little bit. And so, if you as a rookie, you know you're not going to win a championship, so what was my job? To develop him, develop Andrew, develop Zach, and to understand, get them to understand how to play NBA basketball the correct way.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the Timberwolves' ownership transition
quotes.excerpt: Alex Rodriguez and Mark Lore closed on majority ownership and they reached out
quotes.quote: Big transition for us. This wasn't something on our bingo card. About a year ago today, we were celebrating the second Stanley Cup win that we had in Florida in the NHL and Alex Rodriguez and Mark Lore closed on majority ownership and they reached out. It was very humbling. Literally, we were celebrating like on the beach with the Stanley Cup and like that that Monday, they gave me a call saying they would love to chat with me. And the owner that I worked for in Florida was very close to. I worked with him before sports. He's been like a second father to me and he's like, listen, this is a great opportunity. It's new ownership, they want to build a new arena, they're hungry, they have a great, it's a great sports market.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the Timberwolves' arena and market
quotes.excerpt: it's the loudest arena I I've heard. I mean, it's just phenomenal
quotes.quote: It's a great sports market and you know, we don't want to lose you, but what what else more can we accomplish here in Florida? So, talk to my wife about it and you know, she she's from Brazil and the only place she had lived in the US was in South Florida, so this is going to be a big change for her. We just had our third kid, we just bought a house. But when opportunity comes knocking and sometimes you just have to jump on it. So over a two month period, we put it all together, we moved here in September. Everyone's been so welcoming. I mean the Midwest values, the Minnesota nice is real. And another great season, even though we fell short of our goal winning a championship, like the crowds, the the revenue, the sponsorship, all that was was really, really wonderful. And like I mentioned when I spoke to the um to the fans today, like it's the loudest arena I I've heard. I mean, it's just phenomenal.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the process of building a new arena
quotes.excerpt: The whole process has to start multiple years out. You have to coordinate with Nike
quotes.quote: The whole process has to start multiple years out. You have to coordinate with Nike, the league, you have to go through a whole intellectual property process to make sure you're not taking marks from another jersey that someone has IP rights on. So it's a real three year process. A lot of this was done before I arrived. And team owners and business and marketing people have to plan ahead and see how it's going to be well received, what season to introduce the the new marks, all the ordering and the uniforms. So like there's so much build up.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the jersey leak incident
quotes.excerpt: It was really disheartening because we put so much time into it
quotes.quote: It was really disheartening because we put so much time into it. We wanted, you know, I can tell the fans that they liked the new jerseys, but if they were seeing it for the first time, you you would feel more of like, oh wow, you know. We wanted everyone to savor that moment. But yeah, we uh, no, it did not come from us. We have some suspicions that like someone was able to like hack into our our system, which by the way goes to show how passionate the fan base is that someone figured out a way. But we haven't confirmed it all, but there's there was these internal websites that we had that were only for our our use and you know, we discovered that someone got into them.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the feasibility of a new arena
quotes.excerpt: It's going to be very hard. I mean I've had I've done three of these in my past
quotes.quote: It's going to be very hard. I mean I've had I've done three of these in my past. Not brand new arena, but I did two major renovations with the big real estate district. And then I did a brand new practice facility with the music venue, which was about five acres, which is very sizable. Wasn't as expensive as a new arena, but bottom line is I've done three of these processes in over the last 10 years. And there's always going to be hurdles and you know, especially when you have the the public private partnership, but there's there's nothing that scares me. There's no like showstoppers like, oh I haven't seen this before, this is never going to get done.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the season ticket pricing strategy
quotes.excerpt: I was very vocal that it's a pricing reset, we're not going to see those kind of percentage
quotes.quote: I was very vocal that it's a pricing reset, we're not going to see those kind of percentage increases every year. You know, what's really happened here and I saw it in Florida too, is the team was bad for about 20 years, more or less, and pricing was at the bottom of the league. And you know, we've now had six straight seasons of playoffs and a lot of times management teams and ownership groups, you know, fill the building up because the team's playing better, but they're not adjusting the pricing. So the the increases that we've done is just about, you know, level setting and getting closer to, you know, we're at a 30 teams, we're 27th in the league in pricing. We might get up to the low 20s, high teens. Like we're not getting anywhere near NBA medians or certainly not top 10 markets.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on his relationship with the ownership group
quotes.excerpt: They're really empowering to me and Tim Connelly. They see Tim and I as their ownership reps
quotes.quote: They're really empowering to me and Tim Connelly. They see Tim and I as their ownership reps on the ground. Tim obviously on the basketball side, me and the business side. I would say Tim and I talk every single day. We talk to each other a lot more and then we bring decisions to Mark and Alex when we feel that they they need um to opine on it. And a lot of times we're the ones chasing them. Like they they're really empowering to us and they don't want to get, you know, they pay us a lot of money and they put us in big big positions, so they want to make sure that we're we're being able to execute. They don't want me to, they don't want to step in and have um them be a friction point to like slow us down.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing the global scale and business models of NBA and NHL
quotes.excerpt: The business sides are pretty similar. Just the scale of the NBA. I mean it blows my mind.
quotes.quote: The business sides are pretty similar. Season tickets, media rights, sponsorships, the major revenue line items, very similar. Just the scale of the NBA. I mean it blows my mind. They're looking at doing a league in Europe, billion dollar plus valuations. NHL was great but the US and Canadian teams are just starting to get over a billion now. They're probably in the high billions now, at least one billion. I mean the global scale, the casual fan.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Accessibility differences between basketball and hockey for casual fans
quotes.excerpt: Basketball is so easy to pick up and I see it with my kids.
quotes.quote: Season ticket holders make up 70% of the arenas in the NHL. It's hard to get single game buyers that aren't like die hard fans. It's hard to just appeal to someone who's just a sports fan. In South Florida, it took us a long time to appeal to someone that knew nothing about hockey. Basketball is so easy to pick up and I see it with my kids. There's a lot of rules in hockey and icing and offsides that makes it confusing.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA player social media engagement versus NHL star power
quotes.excerpt: We have bench players that have more social media followers than like the stars in the NHL.
quotes.quote: We have bench players that have more social media followers than the stars that we had in the NHL. I know Rob Dillingham's no longer with us, but his social media engagement was more than Connor McDavid or Sasha Barkov in the NHL. It goes to show you that even though he wasn't playing much, just the way he appealed to fans is his lifestyle brand that he had.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the future of regional sports broadcasting
quotes.excerpt: the days of having this cable, you know, RSNs that are changing naming rights every couple years
quotes.quote: The NBA's been vocal about this. There's 13 teams right now, we're one of them, that were on FanDuel this past season. FanDuel's, you know, not going to be existing for next year. Um for next season for sure, there'll be, you know, another option. We haven't announced it yet. We're still digging in on a couple of things. But for the year after, for the 27-28, the league is working tirelessly to consolidate all 13 teams that were on the old, used to be Fox Sports, you know, now is FanDuel, to be on one streaming platform. It's not official, it's not, you know, been finalized, but something like YouTube or Amazon or ESPN, you know, apps. So the way you watch national games would would also be brought to the the local media space. So it would be much, much easier for fans. Um so you don't have to check, you know, every, I know there can be a lot of different, you know, streaming options for where the games are at, but keep in mind, you know, these big media deals that the leagues are getting is the reason why we're able to increase the salary cap and have more revenue and all. So I know there's some friction points, but you know, the days of having this cable, you know, RSNs that are changing naming rights every couple years and going out of business like that's a thing of the past. Like the streaming is definitely the future.
